b2b-targeted-lead-list:
Building an outbound list that a sales team can use

This assignment was not a volume exercise. The goal was to give a B2B agency or SaaS sales team a dependable starting point for outbound work: companies that fit an agreed ideal customer profile, the right decision-makers within those companies, and contact data that has been checked before it reaches a campaign. That focus matters because a large spreadsheet is not automatically a useful prospect list.

Start with fit, including who to leave out

The research began by turning the ideal customer profile into working rules. Industry, company type, geography, team size and likely need were considered alongside explicit disqualifiers. Defining exclusions up front prevents time being spent on businesses that look similar on paper but are not commercially relevant. It also gives a sales team a clear basis for reviewing why a company was included.

Company records were assembled from LinkedIn, Google Maps and relevant directories, then reviewed rather than copied blindly. For each viable company, the work moved from account-level research to the people most likely to own, influence or evaluate the service. Titles were checked for relevance, and the source of the contact information was retained so the delivered data had a traceable research trail.

Make every row usable at the point of outreach

Email addresses passed through a verification workflow before delivery, with risky records clearly separated from safer ones. De-duplication and standardized fields made the file easier to import into a spreadsheet or CRM without creating multiple versions of the same contact. The list also included short personalization hooks, giving outreach writers a practical observation to develop rather than a blank opening line.

The recorded outcome is a clean, organized database with decision-maker titles, verified email status, source notes and personalization context on each row. It is intentionally a handoff for outbound preparation, not a claim that an email sequence has already produced meetings or revenue. Campaign copy, sending reputation and follow-up still determine what happens after the list is used.

custom-business-website:
A custom website designed to earn an inquiry quickly

For this local professional-services website, the brief was to make a visitor understand the offer and trust the business within seconds, whether they arrived from search or a referral. The site therefore had to be fast, clear on a phone and credible without a heavy theme or page builder obscuring the message. It was planned as a business tool first, not as a collection of decorative effects.

Structure gave each page one job

The sitemap separated the questions a prospective customer is likely to ask: what the business does, why it is a credible choice, how its services are organized, what an engagement may cost and how to make contact. Home, Services, About, Pricing and Contact were given distinct roles rather than repeating the same introduction. This information architecture helped the journey move from first impression to inquiry without forcing a visitor to hunt for essentials.

Every page was built with semantic HTML, one primary page heading and a logical heading order. Unique titles, descriptions and Open Graph metadata made the site easier to interpret in search and when shared. The on-page SEO setup is deliberately foundational: it supports discovery and comprehension, but does not promise rankings that depend on competition, content, authority and ongoing work.

Lean code supported the trust message

The design was coded in HTML, CSS and JavaScript from scratch, with mobile-first breakpoints spanning small phones through wide desktop displays. Compressed imagery, descriptive filenames and alternative text kept visual assets purposeful. The contact form was built with validation, while XML sitemap and robots.txt files created the basic technical route for search crawlers. Small scroll-reveal touches were paired with reduced-motion support so the interface stays considerate rather than distracting.

The delivered outcome is a complete, accessible raw-code website with a responsive layout, clear contact path and page-by-page SEO foundations. It creates a stronger platform for a professional service brand; it does not make unsupported claims about traffic or inquiry volumes after launch.

google-ads-search-campaign:
A search campaign blueprint built around real buying intent

This project planned a Google Search Ads account before spend was scaled. The objective was to capture people actively looking for a service while giving the client a disciplined way to learn which searches deserve budget. The work is a production-ready blueprint, not a report of live campaign returns: its value is in the account decisions made before ads begin competing in an auction.

Search terms were organized by intent, not by a loose keyword list

Keyword research was mapped into tight ad groups so that the query, ad message and landing-page promise could stay closely aligned. The initial match-type approach favored phrase match with clear expansion rules, providing control while data is still limited. A negative keyword list was just as important: employment searches, research-only intent, irrelevant locations and other poor-fit queries were identified as exclusions to reduce avoidable waste.

Responsive search ad variants were written around the language of the searcher and the offer’s strongest proof points. Where it made sense, keyword insertion could reinforce relevance without producing awkward copy. Sitelinks, callouts and structured snippets were planned to answer common questions directly in the results page and to create more useful paths to high-intent pages.

Measurement was treated as part of the campaign, not an afterthought

The plan connected conversion tracking and lead-value assignment to the decision of what counts as a meaningful response. Budget pacing and a recurring optimization schedule set expectations for what should be reviewed: search terms, negative keywords, ad combinations, spend distribution and conversion quality. That routine keeps the account from being treated as a “set and forget” channel.

The outcome recorded here is a structured campaign plan with keyword-to-ad-group mapping, negative controls, ad assets, tracking requirements and a budget-review cadence. Actual cost per lead and return depend on factors outside the blueprint, including the offer, landing page, market, bids and sales follow-up.

high-converting-landing-page-design:
Turning campaign clicks into a single clear next step

Paid traffic arrives with limited patience. This landing-page project was designed around that fact: one offer, one audience and one primary action instead of a general-purpose website page that asks a visitor to decide where to go next. The goal was to give Google or Meta Ads traffic a message-matched destination that explains the value, answers likely objections and makes it simple to become a lead.

The page follows the decision a visitor is trying to make

The first screen pairs a direct headline and supporting line with one unmistakable call to action. From there, the page moves through a deliberate sequence: the problem being solved, the offer, the proof available, the questions that might block action and the next invitation to respond. This structure gives every section a reason to exist. It avoids sending a paid visitor through unrelated navigation when the campaign already has a defined goal.

Form design focused on qualification without needless friction. Minimal fields and inline validation keep the submission process understandable, while a WhatsApp route offers an alternative for prospects who would rather start a conversation immediately. Social-proof and testimonial areas were structured so approved evidence can support the decision rather than being treated as visual filler.

Speed and mobile behavior protected the campaign investment

The custom HTML, CSS and JavaScript build kept the page within a lightweight asset budget. Layouts were checked at 360px, 390px, 768px and larger screens because many ad clicks happen on phones, where a cramped form or slow image can end the journey before the offer is read. The content hierarchy, touch targets and form flow were considered together instead of treating mobile as a later resize.

The delivered result is a focused campaign page: message-matched above the fold, built with a friction-conscious lead form, contact alternative and responsive performance discipline. It provides a better place to send paid traffic, while conversion rate still depends on the offer, audience, creative, competition and follow-up process.

keyword-research-content-mapping:
A keyword plan that prevents content from competing with itself

The purpose of this project was to replace topic guesswork with a usable content and SEO roadmap. Rather than handing over an unfiltered list of phrases, the work mapped valuable searches to the one page most able to satisfy them. That gives a client a clearer order of operations: which existing pages need attention, which new pages have a defensible role and which ideas should wait.

Research began with the customer’s language and the search results

Seed topics were expanded across services, customer problems and comparison questions. Each term was classified by informational, commercial or transactional intent, then considered alongside difficulty and funnel stage. Long-tail opportunities received particular attention because a newer or less authoritative domain often benefits from precise, useful topics before it tries to compete for broad head terms.

SERP observation added context that a keyword volume figure cannot supply. The visible formats, competing page types, recurring subtopics and apparent search purpose informed whether a term belonged in a service page, guide, comparison, FAQ or a supporting section. This prevents a content calendar from being based solely on numbers detached from what people actually see when they search.

One primary home for each meaningful topic

The mapping process checked for cannibalization and assigned each priority term to exactly one primary URL. Existing pages could be strengthened where their purpose already matched; new content was reserved for genuine gaps. A six-month calendar then turned that map into an achievable sequence, with an internal-linking plan connecting deeper educational material back to the appropriate commercial or service page.

The documented outcome is a filterable keyword-to-page map with intent, difficulty and priority noted for the client’s language and market. It is a planning asset, not a promise that every target will rank. Publishing quality, technical condition, competition and the site’s existing authority still affect search performance.

local-seo-growth-system:
A local search system built for calls, directions and confidence

Local search is not one isolated task. A service business may appear in Google Maps, organic service results and branded searches, and each of those moments needs consistent business information and a useful answer. This project brought those pieces into one six-month local SEO roadmap so a client could work from a documented system rather than make occasional, disconnected edits.

The plan separates diagnosis from action

A visibility audit established the starting point across local search. Local keyword research then paired real service language with the target city, creating a practical view of the queries that service pages and Google Business Profile information should address. The aim was not to repeat a city name everywhere, but to make location, service scope and contact information unmistakable for nearby customers.

Google Business Profile work covered categories, services, photos and posts, with a checklist for information that should remain accurate over time. NAP consistency and local citation checks supported the same identity across relevant listings. On the site, recommended service-page changes gave local-intent searches a page that matches their need instead of relying entirely on a profile listing.

Reviews and reporting made the system maintainable

The roadmap also outlined a responsible review-request and response approach. Reviews cannot be manufactured, but a business can make it easier for genuine customers to share feedback and can respond professionally when they do. Monthly tracking for rankings, calls and direction requests created a repeatable review point, allowing future local efforts to be based on observed movement rather than vague impressions.

The outcome is a local SEO plan containing an audit, city-and-service keyword map, Business Profile recommendations, citation checklist, review process and reporting template. It provides the framework for ongoing execution; it does not claim a guaranteed map position, since proximity, competition, relevance and profile activity remain variable.

meta-ads-lead-campaign:
A Meta lead-generation structure ready to test responsibly

This case study covers the planning of a Meta Ads lead-generation system before the client’s budget is scaled. The goal was to give Facebook and Instagram campaigns a clean structure for reaching cold audiences, continuing conversations with warm visitors and measuring which creative and audiences generate qualified responses. The ad account and budget remain client-owned, keeping the investment and visibility with the business.

Campaign stages were separated on purpose

The account architecture distinguished cold prospecting, warm activity and retargeting rather than combining every audience inside one campaign. This separation makes it easier to see what is introducing a new audience to the offer and what is bringing previous visitors back. Ideal-customer-profile work informed the audience layers, but the plan left room for results to guide future exclusions and expansions instead of assuming an initial interest set is perfect.

Creative was treated as a testable sales message, not just a design task. A structured calendar outlined different angles to test against the same audience: problem awareness, offer clarity, proof, urgency or common objections. Testing one meaningful variable at a time helps a team learn more than a constant stream of unrelated ads, and prevents early opinions from being mistaken for performance evidence.

Lead quality and measurement were designed into the handoff

Lead-form qualification questions were included to reduce clearly unsuitable responses before they enter a sales workflow. The pixel and conversion-event checklist gave the account a measurement foundation, while retargeting sequences addressed page visitors and form abandoners who may need a second encounter with the offer. A weekly optimization and reporting routine defined when to assess lead quality, creative fatigue, spend and event data.

The project outcome is a complete campaign build with audience architecture, creative test plan, qualification approach and tracking setup ready before scaling. It does not claim a final cost per lead or volume of qualified leads; those results depend on the offer, creative, market, follow-up speed and live account data.

photographer-portfolio-website:
A gallery-first portfolio that keeps the work in focus

A visual professional needs a website that lets the work carry the first impression without making a potential client wait for it. This portfolio build was planned for photographers, videographers and design studios that need fast image-led browsing and an uncomplicated route to a booking inquiry. The interface stays deliberately quiet so the gallery, not a busy template, holds attention.

Gallery architecture balanced impact with loading discipline

The masonry-style gallery was built to accommodate varied image shapes while maintaining an intentional rhythm across screens. Images lazy-load so that a visitor does not have to download the entire body of work before seeing the first pieces. Lightweight vanilla JavaScript avoided adding a slider library simply for movement, keeping the technical stack aligned with the performance requirements of an image-heavy site.

The responsive grid was considered from phone to desktop. On small screens the browsing experience still needs enough image presence to feel like a portfolio, while navigation and contact controls must remain easy to reach. About and booking sections supply the context that a gallery alone cannot: who the creator is, what they offer and how to take the next step.

Images also need understandable signals for search

Image SEO was incorporated through descriptive filenames, useful alternative text and structured captions. Those details help search systems and visitors who use assistive technology understand what a visual represents without turning the page into a keyword list. They also give a creator a more maintainable publishing standard as new work is added to the site.

The delivered outcome is a custom-coded, gallery-led portfolio with responsive behavior, image-optimization strategy, minimal navigation and a simple inquiry path. It is built to support booking conversations, while actual booking volume will naturally depend on the portfolio, positioning, pricing, audience and ongoing promotion.

prospect-research-data-cleaning:
Turning an unreliable prospect sheet into a campaign-ready asset

Existing prospect data often has more value than it first appears, but only if a team can tell which records are safe to use. This project began with a disorganized client spreadsheet containing duplicates, inconsistent company names and addresses that could no longer be trusted. The objective was to rebuild that file into a clean, verified and clearly structured database for an outreach or CRM workflow.

The audit exposed the problems before they were overwritten

The first pass looked for duplicate contacts, malformed email syntax, missing fields and inconsistent conventions. Company names were normalized so variations such as “Ltd”, “Limited” and “Ltd.” did not create artificial duplicates. Phone numbers were formatted with country codes to make records more usable across markets and communication tools. This is detailed work, but it protects later segmentation and reporting from being built on mismatched data.

Email verification separated likely deliverable addresses from bounced or risky records. Rather than silently deleting questionable data, the process preserved a usable status so a client can understand why a record was handled differently. That transparency is important when sales teams need to decide whether a contact should be researched again, retained for another channel or removed from an email sequence.

The delivery format supported the next operational step

Columns were standardized for CRM import, and lifecycle fields—new, contacted, replied and disqualified—gave the client a simple starting structure for follow-up. Re-organization was not just a visual clean-up; it was intended to reduce import errors, prevent repeated outreach and make a batch easier to assign. The before-and-after view documented the cleaning and verification treatment applied to the list.

The stated outcome is a cleaned and organized prospect database with verification flags and campaign-ready fields. It does not guarantee inbox placement or replies, because sending reputation, outreach copy, consent practices and timing still matter once the file is activated.

social-media-design-pack:
A social design system that makes everyday publishing easier

Small businesses often need to publish regularly without waiting for a designer to create every post from scratch. This project addressed that operational need by creating a reusable social-media design system: consistent enough to feel like one recognizable brand, but flexible enough for routine posts, stories, announcements and promotions. The goal was dependable day-to-day output, not a one-off collection of attractive graphics.

The visual rules came before individual templates

Color, typography and layout decisions were established as a compact direction system. These rules make it easier to recognize the brand even when the subject of a post changes, and they give staff a useful reference when they need to create new material. Defining the system first also reduces the common drift that happens when each post is designed independently with a different font, color balance or style of imagery.

The resulting template set covered Facebook and Instagram posts, story layouts, announcement formats and promotional offers. Each layout was designed around a repeatable message hierarchy so that an important offer, date or call to action does not disappear under decoration. Templates are a guardrail, not a restriction: they allow a team to vary content while retaining the cues followers learn to recognize.

Handoff guidance helped the system survive beyond launch

Export guidance balanced visual quality with file-size discipline, helping staff choose formats that look clear once uploaded. A simple usage guide showed how to reuse the templates so the client did not receive files without a process. This makes the design pack more practical for an owner or team member who needs to publish quickly while still protecting brand consistency.

The outcome is a reusable set of social templates and a straightforward handoff guide for a small business. It supports a more coherent publishing presence, but it does not make unsupported claims about follower growth or engagement; results also depend on the content, offer, frequency, audience and community management.

technical-seo-audit-report:
A technical SEO audit that turns issues into an implementation order

This technical SEO audit was designed to identify the site conditions that can quietly limit search visibility and conversion paths. The output was not a list of unexplained warnings. It was a plain-language report that connected crawlability, indexation, metadata, speed, structured data and page structure to a prioritized fix roadmap a developer or site owner can actually use.

Crawl and indexation checks came first

The review examined broken links, redirects and redirect chains, then moved into indexation questions such as noindex directives, canonical signals and duplicate versions. These issues can interfere with which URL a search engine sees as the useful version of a page. Documenting them early means content or link-building efforts are less likely to be layered over a site that still has basic access and consolidation problems.

Metadata, heading hierarchy and semantic structure were reviewed in the context of what each page is intended to communicate. Missing or duplicated titles and descriptions may be straightforward fixes, but the report also considered whether the page uses headings and markup in a way that makes its main subject understandable. Structured-data gaps were translated into JSON-LD recommendations where the page type and available information made those enhancements appropriate.

Performance findings were connected to priority

Page-speed diagnostics considered Core Web Vitals, including LCP, INP and CLS, rather than treating a single score as the entire story. The final roadmap organized findings by impact and effort so teams can distinguish urgent technical barriers from useful refinements. This order gives a developer a realistic way to schedule work and gives a client a clear explanation of why one fix should happen before another.

The recorded outcome is a full technical SEO report with each issue, recommended fix, priority and expected technical effect explained in accessible language. A technical audit can reduce barriers, but it cannot guarantee rankings because relevance, competition, content quality, authority and implementation quality continue to influence search results.

youtube-thumbnail-design-set:
A thumbnail system that earns attention before the video begins

A YouTube thumbnail has to communicate the promise of a video in a very small space, often while competing against many other visual options on a mobile screen. This project created a thumbnail set for an education or creator channel with two linked goals: make each topic immediately understandable and make the overall series recognizable as viewers encounter new uploads.

Readability determined the composition

Typography was selected and arranged for mobile-scale legibility, where long headlines and fine details quickly disappear. Each thumbnail was planned around a clear focal point, purposeful contrast and a limited amount of text. That decision is not simply aesthetic: when the viewer cannot identify the subject or visual priority at a glance, even a strong video idea can be overlooked.

Consistency was built as a reusable series system rather than copied as one fixed composition. Shared color cues, type treatment and layout logic help returning viewers recognize the channel, while the focal image and message can change to fit the individual video. This preserves variety without sacrificing the memory cues a content series needs.

Variants made room for evidence instead of preference

A/B layout variants were prepared to explore different concepts without abandoning the central visual system. These alternatives give the channel an organized way to test what is clearest or most compelling for a particular topic. Export presets ensured files meet YouTube requirements consistently, avoiding last-minute resizing or quality problems in the publishing workflow.

The delivered outcome is a thumbnail design set that is mobile-readable, contrast-led and consistent across a series, with export presets ready for use. It is designed to support stronger click-through decisions; it does not claim a particular CTR because topic, title, audience, competition and distribution also shape that metric.
